concept: A link in the text colour found by its underline, because Pane owns no hue and a link must still be told apart from text.

default_to_avoid.pattern: a blue underlined link (the browser default, Material link)
default_to_avoid.why_not: blue is a hue the system does not own (D-024); an underline does the finding without one

derivation.consequence: the scene supplies the hue; the system owns no hue of its own, only white at opacities and one ink, and colour appears only where it states a status or marks a diagram
derivation.form: the link is the text colour with a quiet underline; the underline, not a hue, says it is a link

derivation.consequence: keyboard reaches everything a pointer can, with a visible focus ring on any backdrop
derivation.form: a focus ring on the link like every control, on any backdrop

derivation.consequence: secondary text keeps the lowest opacity that still measured as passing; text halos count only where WCAG allows them
derivation.form: the underline sits below the baseline so descenders stay readable

variants.reason: A finds the link without a hue (P1) and meets 1.4.1 by its underline. B brings back the blue the user rejected (R-012). C makes a sentence full of buttons.

root.why: the text colour with an underline offset below the baseline so descenders stay clear

inline.why: in a sentence the underline is always there, quiet, so the link is found without a hue

standalone.why: on its own line the weight marks it, the underline arrives on hover, and the line is a 44px target

sr.why: words for a screen reader that the link opens a new tab, never shown

hover.why: the underline darkens and thickens at hover pace, an answer to the pointer

focus-visible.why: the shared focus ring so a keyboard user sees where they are

@media forced-colors: active.why: forced colours use the system link colour, the same in every theme and on every scene

text-decoration-color.why: the underline colour eases at hover pace with the pointer
